Gives Oracle's decline since its September high as of early February 2026.

receipt.public_excerpt: Months after Oracle's (ORCL) $400 billion-plus contract backlog ignited a stock-market frenzy, the enthusiasm has given way to doubts about its reliance on OpenAI and debt-fueled datacenter buildout

evidence_items.explanation: Reuters reports that the frenzy over Oracle's September backlog gave way to investor doubts about OpenAI reliance and debt. The same story says the stock erased its September 10 gains.

receipt.public_excerpt: The stock is down almost 12% in just five days, and more than half its value has been wiped out since its September high.

evidence_items.explanation: By the day before the post, Oracle had lost more than half its value since its September high, consistent with lost confidence after the September deal.

evidence_items.publisher: Fortune (reporting Bank of America Global Fund Manager Survey)

receipt.public_excerpt: a net 20% of FMS investors now believe companies are deploying capital too aggressively—a sentiment not observed since August 2005. This dramatic shift is explicitly linked to the “magnitude & financing of the AI capex boom,”

evidence_items.explanation: A November 2025 survey of professional investors showed a sharp turn to worry about AI spending and its financing.

receipt.public_excerpt: Nvidia has become the first company to reach $5 trillion in market value amid a global artificial intelligence arms race.

evidence_items.explanation: Seven weeks after the Oracle deal, Nvidia reached a record value. Confidence in the AI trade did not drop right away.

evidence_items.publisher: Fortune (reporting Bank of America Global Fund Manager Survey)

receipt.public_excerpt: Overall investor sentiment, based on cash levels, equity allocation, and global growth expectations, rose to its highest level since February 2025.

evidence_items.explanation: Broad investor sentiment stayed high in November 2025. Under a whole-market reading, this cuts against a general loss of confidence.

unresolved_gaps: No single measure of 'Wall Street confidence' exists; the result depends on reading it as confidence in the AI trade rather than the whole market.
Whether Marcus called the Oracle deal 'peak bubble' at the time was not checked, since only his own writing would show it.
